title: Abba Bira’ah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman finds him mentioned only once, in Menachot 93b: “It was taught: Abba Bira’ah son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,” etc. Seder HaDorot, under the entry Bira’ah, is uncertain whether he was the son of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov or spoke in his name. Hyman firmly proposes a small correction in the books, following Dikdukei Soferim: “for Abba Bira’ah recited a baraita.” Hyman explains that Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov also arranged baraitot, as cited in the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 1, chapter 6. In Hyman’s explanation, this Abba Bira’ah brought one baraita from the baraitot of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. Bira’ah is a town-name, as in Megillah 4a, Ulla Bira’ah, and Rashi explains: from Biri.

notes.text: Hyman rejects the initial son/in-the-name-of ambiguity by proposing דתני אבא ביראה: a reciter transmitting a baraita. The opening genealogy-shaped quotation is preserved as his received text, not adopted as a father/son fact. Megillah4a has Ulla Biraah.

The consulted Menachot 93b directly has Abba Biraah be-Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov. The separately consulted Megillah 4a has Ulla Biraah and is a place-name parallel, not evidence that Ulla and Abba are identical. Hyman’s proposed reciter/baraita reading, town-name explanation and exact Dikdukei Soferim/Iggeret reports remain his argument.
